How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step walkthrough for generating a **RESTful API request** in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard (v6.3.1)** for the API named **“get information of device connector versions.”** The instructions assume you already have access to a running Nexus Dashboard instance and that you’re logged in with a role that has API‑Explorer privileges. --- ## 1. Locate the API in the Nexus Dashboard UI | Step | Action | Screenshot (optional) | |------|--------|-----------------------| | 1 | Open your browser and navigate to the Nexus Dashboard URL (e.g., `https:///`). | ![Login](https://example.com/login.png) | | 2 | Log in with your credentials. | ![Dashboard](https://example.com/dashboard.png) | | 3 | In the left‑hand navigation pane, click **“API Explorer”** (or “Developer Tools → API Explorer”). | ![API Explorer](https://example.com/api-explorer.png) | | 4 | In the API Explorer search bar, type **“device connector versions”** or the exact API name “get information of device connector versions.” | ![Search](https://example.com/search.png) | | 5 | Click the matching entry in the results list. | ![Select API](https://example.com/select-api.png) | > **Tip:** If the API isn’t listed, ensure that the **Device Connector** service is enabled and that your user role has permission to view it. --- ## 2. Inspect the API Definition Once you’ve selected the API, the right‑hand panel will display its details: | Section | What you’ll see | How to use it | |---------|-----------------|---------------| | **Endpoint** | `/api/v1/device_connector/versions` (example path) | This is the URL you’ll hit. | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | Use this verb in your request. | | **Parameters** | *None* (for this particular API) | No query or path parameters required. | | **Headers** | `Accept: application/json`
`Authorization: Bearer ` | Include these headers. | | **Response Schema** | JSON object describing connector versions | Helps you understand the payload. | > **Note:** The actual endpoint may differ slightly; always copy the exact URL shown in the UI. --- ## 3. Generate the Request ### 3.1 Using the Built‑in “Generate Request” Button | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | With the API definition open, click the **“Generate Request”** button at the top of the panel. | | 2 | A modal dialog appears showing the full HTTP request ready to copy. | | 3 | Copy the request text (including method, URL, headers, and body). | | 4 | Paste it into your preferred tool (curl, Postman, etc.). | > **Example output** (the modal will show something like this): ``` GET https:///api/v1/device_connector/versions Accept: application/json Authorization: Bearer ``` ### 3.2 Using the “Try It Out” Feature If you want to execute the request directly from the UI: | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Click **“Try It Out”**. | | 2 | The UI will automatically send the request and display the raw response below. | | 3 | You can view the status code, headers, and body. | | 4 | Optionally, click **“Save Response”** to export the data. | --- ## 4. Execute the Request via cURL (Command Line) ```bash # Replace and accordingly curl -X GET \ https:///api/v1/device_connector/versions \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` > **Output Example** ```json { "connectorVersions": [ { "name": "ConnectorA", "version": "1.0.3", "status": "active" }, { "name": "ConnectorB", "version": "2.1.0", "status": "deprecated" } ] } ``` --- ## 5. Execute the Request via Postman (GUI) 1. **Create a new request** in Postman. 2. Set the method to **GET**. 3. Enter the full URL: `https:///api/v1/device_connector/versions`. 4. Under **Headers**, add: - `Accept: application/json` - `Authorization: Bearer ` 5. Hit **Send**. 6. View the response in the **Body** tab. --- ## 6. Automate the Request (Python Example) If you prefer to script the call, here’s a minimal Python snippet using `requests`: ```python import requests url = "https:///api/v1/device_connector/versions" headers = { "Accept": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}" } response = requests.get(url, headers=headers) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` > **Tip:** Store the token securely (e.g., environment variable, vault). --- ## 7. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Token expired or missing | Refresh the token or re‑authenticate. | | **404 Not Found** | Wrong endpoint path | Verify the URL in the API Explorer. | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Backend issue | Check Nexus Dashboard logs or contact support. | | **No Parameters Listed** | API truly requires none | Proceed without adding query strings. | --- ## 8. Summary Checklist - [ ] Logged into Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1. - [ ] Navigated to **API Explorer**. - [ ] Located the **“get information of device connector versions”** API. - [ ] Copied the generated request (method, URL, headers). - [ ] Executed via UI, cURL, Postman, or script.
